**Seminar**

## Problem 10.1. Build the matrix from three hints

Work in the first approximation: $U_{e3}=0$, the atmospheric mixing angle
is close to $45^\circ$, and the matrix may be chosen real.

1. For high-energy solar neutrinos take
   $P_{ee}\simeq1/3$. For an adiabatic exit from the Sun this gives
   $|U_{e2}|^2\simeq1/3$. Using the normalization of the electron row,
   fill in $|U_{e1}|^2$ and $|U_{e3}|^2$.
2. Atmospheric disappearance is described in the leading approximation by the depth
   $4|U_{\mu3}|^2(1-|U_{\mu3}|^2)\simeq1$. Find $|U_{\mu3}|^2$.
   Fill in $|U_{\tau3}|^2$ from the normalization of the third column.
3. Choose the same signs for $U_{\mu3}$ and $U_{\tau3}$. What does the
   orthogonality of the second and third columns say about the relation between
   $U_{\mu2}$ and $U_{\tau2}$? Normalize the second column and fill in
   $|U_{\mu2}|^2$, $|U_{\tau2}|^2$.
4. Use the normalizations of the two remaining rows. Show that

   $$
   |U_0|^2=
   \begin{pmatrix}
   2/3&1/3&0\\
   1/6&1/3&1/2\\
   1/6&1/3&1/2
   \end{pmatrix}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-manual-matrix}

5. Choose the signs of the elements so that the resulting real matrix
   $U_0$ satisfies $U_0^{\mathsf T}U_0=I$. Write out all three ones
   and all six zeros in the product.
6. Which entry does the reactor result $|U_{e3}|^2\simeq0.0225$ change
   first? Explain which conclusions of the approximate matrix remain
   qualitatively correct. Can this construction be used to independently check
   unitarity, if it was used at every step?

## Problem 10.2. How to read the PMNS matrix

Use the standard factorization

$$
U=R_{23}U_{13}(\delta)R_{12}.
$$ {#eq-ex10-001}

1. Multiply the matrices and obtain the first row and the third column of $U$.
2. Prove the relations

   $$
   |U_{e3}|=\sin\theta_{13},
   \qquad
   \frac{|U_{e2}|}{|U_{e1}|}=\tan\theta_{12},
   \qquad
   \frac{|U_{\mu3}|}{|U_{\tau3}|}=\tan\theta_{23}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-002}

3. For the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering use

   $$
   \sin^2\theta_{12}=0.3088,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{23}=0.470,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{13}=0.02248
   $$ {#eq-ex10-003}

   and compute
   $|U_{e1}|$, $|U_{e2}|$, $|U_{e3}|$, $|U_{\mu3}|$ and $|U_{\tau3}|$.
4. Explain why the phase $\delta$ becomes unobservable at
   $s_{13}=0$.
5. An arbitrary unitary matrix $3\times3$ contains three angles and six
   phases. Count how many phases can be removed by rephasing the fields in
   the Dirac case.
6. For the Majorana case set

   $$
   \widetilde U
   =U\operatorname{diag}
   \left(1,e^{i\alpha_{21}/2},e^{i\alpha_{31}/2}\right).
   $$ {#eq-ex10-004}

   Show that the additional phases cancel in the product
   $\widetilde U_{\beta i}\widetilde U_{\alpha i}^*$ and therefore do not enter the
   oscillation probabilities.

**Homework**

## Problem 10.3. General three-flavor probability

For three active neutrinos

$$
|\nu_\alpha\rangle
=\sum_{i=1}^3U_{\alpha i}^*|\nu_i\rangle.
$$ {#eq-ex10-005}

1. Carry out the evolution of the mass components and obtain the ultrarelativistic
   amplitude

   $$
   \mathcal A_{\alpha\to\beta}(L,E)
   =\sum_iU_{\beta i}U_{\alpha i}^*
   \exp\!\left(-i\frac{m_i^2L}{2E}\right).
   $$ {#eq-ex10-006}

2. Square the amplitude and obtain a double sum over $i,j$.
3. Combine the terms $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$, introduce

   $$
   X_{\alpha\beta}^{ij}
   =U_{\alpha i}^*U_{\beta i}
    U_{\alpha j}U_{\beta j}^*,
   \qquad
   \Delta_{ij}=\frac{\Delta m_{ij}^2L}{4E},
   $$ {#eq-ex10-007}

   and derive the general probability formula in terms of
   $\operatorname{Re}X^{ij}$ and $\operatorname{Im}X^{ij}$.
4. Obtain the formula for the survival probability $P_{\alpha\to\alpha}$.
5. Using the unitarity $U$, prove

   $$
   \sum_\beta P_{\alpha\to\beta}=1
   $$ {#eq-ex10-008}

   and show that for $L=0$
   $P_{\alpha\to\beta}=\delta_{\alpha\beta}$.
6. Show how the general formula reduces to the two-flavor one if one
   mass component does not participate.
7. Prove

   $$
   \Delta m_{31}^2=\Delta m_{32}^2+\Delta m_{21}^2
   $$ {#eq-ex10-009}

   and explain why only two oscillation frequencies are independent.
8. Perform the replacement $m_i^2\to m_i^2+C$. Show that the amplitude acquires
   only an overall phase factor, while the probability does not change.
9. Which experiments, unlike oscillations, are sensitive to the absolute
   scale of neutrino masses?

## Problem 10.4. CP violation and the Jarlskog invariant

1. Show that for antineutrinos the oscillation amplitude is obtained
   by the replacement $U\to U^*$.
2. Using the general three-flavor probability, obtain

   $$
   A_{\alpha\beta}^{\mathrm{CP}}
   =P(\nu_\alpha\to\nu_\beta)
   -P(\bar\nu_\alpha\to\bar\nu_\beta)
   =4\sum_{i>j}\operatorname{Im}X_{\alpha\beta}^{ij}
   \sin2\Delta_{ij}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-010}

3. Prove that $A_{\alpha\alpha}^{\mathrm{CP}}=0$ in vacuum.
4. For the quartet

   $$
   J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   =\operatorname{Im}
   \left(U_{e2}^*U_{\mu2}U_{e1}U_{\mu1}^*\right)
   $$ {#eq-ex10-011}

   check the invariance under rephasing of the rows and columns of the mixing
   matrix.
5. From the standard PMNS parametrization obtain

   $$
   J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   =\frac18
   \sin2\theta_{12}\sin2\theta_{23}\sin2\theta_{13}
   \cos\theta_{13}\sin\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-012}

6. Using $\Delta_{31}=\Delta_{32}+\Delta_{21}$ and trigonometric
   identities, derive

   $$
   A_{e\mu}^{\mathrm{CP}}
   =16J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   \sin\Delta_{21}\sin\Delta_{32}\sin\Delta_{31}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-013}

7. List all the conditions under which the vacuum CP asymmetry vanishes.
   Why is there no fundamental CP violation in the two-flavor vacuum
   model?
8. For the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering use

   $$
   \theta_{12}=33.76^\circ,
   \quad
   \theta_{23}=43.29^\circ,
   \quad
   \theta_{13}=8.62^\circ,
   \quad
   \delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=212^\circ
   $$ {#eq-ex10-014}

   and compute $J_{\mathrm{CP}}$.
9. Estimate $A_{e\mu}^{\mathrm{CP}}$ at the first atmospheric maximum,
   defined by the condition $\Delta_{31}=\pi/2$. Use

   $$
   \Delta m_{21}^2=7.537\cdot10^{-5}~\mathrm{eV}^2,
   \qquad
   \Delta m_{31}^2=2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-015}

   Why is the asymmetry additionally suppressed by the smallness of the solar phase?

## Problem 10.5. Numerical lab of three flavors

Write a program in Python, Julia, or Mathematica that computes vacuum
oscillations of three active neutrinos. For Python you can use the
[template](https://neutrinohit.github.io/neutrinophysics/introduction/ru/exercises/assets/09_vacuum_oscillations/three_flavor_starter.en.py).

Use the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin^2\theta_{12}&=0.3088,&
\sin^2\theta_{23}&=0.470,&
\sin^2\theta_{13}&=0.02248,\\
\Delta m_{21}^2&=7.537\cdot10^{-5}~\mathrm{eV}^2,&
\Delta m_{31}^2&=2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2,&
\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}&=212^\circ.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ex10-016}

1. Construct the PMNS matrix in the standard parametrization and numerically check
   $U^\dagger U=I$.
2. Implement the amplitude $\mathcal A_{\alpha\to\beta}$. If the rows
   denote the final flavor $\beta$ and the columns the initial flavor $\alpha$,
   then in matrix form

   $$
   \mathcal A
   =U\operatorname{diag}(e^{-i\phi_i})U^\dagger,
   \qquad
   \phi_i=2(1.267)\frac{m_i^2[\mathrm{eV}^2]L[\mathrm{km}]}
                              {E[\mathrm{GeV}]}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-017}

   One can set $m_1^2=0$, since the overall mass is not observable.
3. Compute the probability matrix $P_{\beta\alpha}=|\mathcal A_{\beta\alpha}|^2$.
4. Automatically check

   $$
   P_{\beta\alpha}(0)=\delta_{\beta\alpha},
   \qquad
   \sum_\beta P_{\beta\alpha}=1
   $$ {#eq-ex10-018}

   with a numerical accuracy no worse than $10^{-12}$.
5. For the initial $\nu_\mu$ plot $P_{\mu\to e}$,
   $P_{\mu\to\mu}$ and $P_{\mu\to\tau}$ as functions of $L/E$ in the range
   $0\leq L/E\leq2000~\mathrm{km/GeV}$.
6. Repeat the calculation for antineutrinos, replacing $U\to U^*$, and plot
   $P_{\mu\to e}-\overline P_{\mu\to e}$.
7. Repeat the comparison at $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=0$ and explain the result.
8. Add the same number $C$ to all $m_i^2$ and numerically check
   that the probabilities do not change.
9. By scanning over $L/E$, find the point of the maximal vacuum
   difference $P_{\mu\to e}-\overline P_{\mu\to e}$ in absolute value in the indicated range.
10. Represent the triple of probabilities

    $$
    (P_{\alpha\to e},P_{\alpha\to\mu},P_{\alpha\to\tau})
    $$ {#eq-ex10-019}

    as a trajectory inside the probability triangle. Why can the trajectory not
    leave the triangle?
11. In item 1 the matrix is unitary by construction. What independent
    experimental normalizations and channels would be needed to check
    unitarity without fixing it in the parametrization in advance?

In a real long-baseline experiment the comparison of neutrinos and antineutrinos
is also modified by matter. In this problem only the vacuum part needs to be computed.
